items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: I didn't write 99 plus one. Wardell wrote the tune.

ctx.x: Oh, okay. Okay. You did make a record.

We had an office on Arlene Street. And we did the tune, 99 plus one. It made a little noise, it made enough noise for them to come back to make an album. And then at that time, for you to make an album, it had to sell it. And then I didn't get, I didn't write 99 plus one. Wardell wrote the tune. I had a tune on that album called Mustard Greens. As a matter of fact, a friend of mine just gave me an album of it. I really lost that album too. So I have a copy of that. It's mostly instrumental. It's not necessarily a…
Well, I think I've got a copy in the back of 99 plus one.

items.title: Wardel Quezergue Interview, 1995-10-25
items.q: we did an album with Nola Records with June Gardner.

ctx.x: Now which camp, I think Dave came first. Yeah, yeah, definitely. Dave came first. Then these, then this company came in. Nola Records came next. And that's where Barefootin' came into play. That was before Malico, right. That was the only, I got a deal out of that, no, that's not my head of my time. We did that, and then our company was, no, I think that was Nola Records that was the only, we did a Joe Wilson, and we did, we did an album with Nola Records with June Gardner. I don't know if you ever heard of that…
Okay, I, yeah, I remember that. But that was Nola?
